paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage gives you. The man says it all out loud, and the Bible keeps every word. He says, "I am the man who has seen affliction under the rod of God’s wrath," and he never cleans it up (Lamentations 3:1). If you've ever been scared your honest prayer was too much, this is your proof that God's Word has room for it.

Now hear how low he goes. He says, "My strength has perished, along with my hope from the LORD" (Lamentations 3:18). He's not pretending, and I think that's the point. I spent years at the back of a junk drawer, and I can tell you, I think pretending it wasn't dark would have only made me more tired.

And watch where he ends up in these verses. He says, "Remember my affliction and wandering, the wormwood and the gall," and then, "Surely my soul remembers and is humbled within me" (Lamentations 3:19-20). He's still hurting, friend, and he's still talking. The poem isn't over yet, so keep your oven warm and your heart honest.
